display.purpose: The onboarding question and Safe Mode (Outfit 700, 30px). The only 30px on screen.

body.purpose: The default UI voice — buttons, menu items, inputs, list rows (Outfit 500, 14px).

small.purpose: Segmented labels, callout body, scrubber labels (Outfit 500-600, 13px). The floor for functional sans text.

mono.purpose: Keycaps, type chips, knob labels and values (JetBrains Mono 500, 11px). Exact values only.

micro.purpose: Socket labels, ruler marks, unit labels (JetBrains Mono 600, 9.5px, uppercase, 0.08em). Held to the full 4.5:1 body-text bar.

shadows.name: shadow-raised
shadows.purpose: On the ground: key tiles, the selected segment, callouts, banners, the knob dial.

shadows.name: shadow-overlay
shadows.purpose: Above the ground: node cards, menus, modals, popovers, the transport pill.

shadows.name: shadow-inset
shadows.purpose: Recessed into the ground: the port socket well.

shadows.name: shadow-pressed
shadows.purpose: Being hit right now: a lit key tile.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The ONE focus ring. :focus-visible only; stacks over the element own shadow.

shadows.name: cable-signal-glow
shadows.purpose: The only glow in the system, and only in proportion to live audio. Ports never glow.

motion.name: motion-spring
motion.purpose: transform ONLY. The overshoot is the weight.

motion.name: press-scale-btn
motion.purpose: Button press. The box never moves.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: Hover lift, pads and keys only.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Exactly two exemptions: .oj-cable and .oj-meter — they are meters, not decoration.

components.name: Node
components.description: The signature surface: a white card with a 1px hairline and soft layered depth, draggable from its header. Ports are recessed socket wells in the FIRST ROW OF THE BODY — inputs left, outputs right. Used as-is or opened (press E) to rewire its insides.
components.html: Samplerinstrument
components.css: .ds-node { display: inline-block; min-width: 190px; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #E3E1DA; border-radius: 14px; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(24,22,16,.07), 0 12px 28px rgba(24,22,16,.11); font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; color: #1D1C18; } .ds-node-header { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 14px; background: #FAF9F6; border-bottom: 1px solid #E3E1DA; border-radius: 14px 14px 0 0; cursor: grab; } .ds-node-grip { display: inline-grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; gap: 2.5px; } .ds-node-grip i { width: 3px; height: 3px; border-radius: 50%; background: #C8C5BB; } .ds-node-title { font-weight: 600; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.2; } .ds-node-type { margin-left: auto; font-family: "JetBrains Mono", monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .08em; color: #6C695F; background: #ECEAE4; padding: 4px 7px; border-radius: 6px; } .ds-node-body { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding: 12px 14px; } .ds-port-row { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; min-height: 24px; }

components.name: Port socket
components.description: A typed connection point, rendered as an 18px RECESSED WELL inside the node body with an 8px core dot. Idle sockets of every kind read identically; the core takes the wiring colour only when connected. Hover recolours the ring. Ports NEVER glow and never scale.
components.css: .ds-port { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 18px; height: 18px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ECEAE4; border: 1px solid #89867C; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,.22); cursor: crosshair; transition: border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1); } .ds-port i { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: #6C695F; } .ds-port:hover { border-color: oklch(0.66 0.19 40); } .ds-port.is-connected-audio i { background: oklch(0.6 0.12 200); } .ds-port.is-connected-control i { background: #8F8C82; } .ds-port-label { font-family: "JetBrains Mono", monospace; font-size: 9.5px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .08em; color: #6C695F; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Accent-filled primary action with DARK INK label (white on the accent measures 3.36:1). Flat inset construction: no border, no shadow. Compresses to scale(.96) on press; the hover LIFTS the accent rather than darkening it.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1; color: #1D1C18; background: oklch(0.66 0.19 40); border: 0; border-radius: 10px; padding: 9px 16px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1), transform 260ms cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.71 0.19 40); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, oklch(0.66 0.19 40) 28%, transparent); }

components.name: Node Button
components.description: The default button: a flat inset fill, no border, no shadow. Hover mixes 8% ink into the fill; press compresses.
components.css: .ds-btn { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1; color: #1D1C18; background: #ECEAE4; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; padding: 9px 16px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1), transform 260ms cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1); } .ds-btn:hover { background: color-mix(in oklab, #1D1C18 8%, #ECEAE4); } .ds-btn:active { transform: scale(0.96); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, oklch(0.66 0.19 40) 28%, transparent); }

components.name: Input
components.description: Card-fill field with a 1px interactive outline. Focus swaps the border to the accent AND adds the one focus ring. Numeric fields add the mono modifier with tabular-nums.
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1.3; color: #1D1C18; background: #FFFFFF; border: 1px solid #C8C5BB; border-radius: 10px; padding: 9px 12px; transition: border-color 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1), box-shadow 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1); } .ds-input:hover { border-color: #89867C; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: oklch(0.66 0.19 40); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, oklch(0.66 0.19 40) 28%, transparent); } .ds-input--mono { font-family: "JetBrains Mono", monospace; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Knob
components.description: The standard faceplate control. A 52px dial with a top-left light gradient and an accent tick sweeping -135deg..+135deg. The tick has NO transition — it must track the finger exactly. Vertical drag over 150px is a full sweep; it is a real role="slider" with keyboard stepping.
components.html:
cutoff
440 Hz
components.css: .ds-knob { width: 52px; height: 52px; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 35% 30%, #FFFFFF, #ECEAE4); border: 1px solid #89867C; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(24,22,16,.05), 0 2px 6px rgba(24,22,16,.06); position: relative; cursor: grab; } .ds-knob::after { content: ""; position: absolute; top: 4px; left: calc(50% - 1.5px); width: 3px; height: 15px; border-radius: 2px; background: oklch(0.66 0.19 40); transform-origin: 50% 22px; transform: rotate(var(--rot, -135deg)); } .ds-knob:hover, .ds-knob:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(24,22,16,.05), 0 2px 6px rgba(24,22,16,.06), 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in oklab, oklch(0.66 0.19 40) 28%, transparent); } .ds-knob-label, .ds-knob-value { font-family: "JetBrains Mono", monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; text-align: center; } .ds-knob-label { color: #6C695F; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: .08em; } .ds-knob-value { color: #5A5850; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }

components.name: Key Tile
components.description: The playable surface. Rest lifts on hover (-2px), compresses on press (.94), and while HELD fills solid accent with a dark-ink legend, translateY(1px) and the pressed inset shadow — pressed INTO the instrument. No glow.
components.css: .ds-key { width: 48px; height: 48px; border: 1px solid #89867C; border-radius: 10px; background: #FFFFFF; color: #6C695F; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(24,22,16,.05), 0 2px 6px rgba(24,22,16,.06); font: 600 10px/1 "JetBrains Mono", monospace; cursor: pointer; transition: background 120ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.3,1), transform 260ms cubic-bezier(.34,1.56,.64,1); } .ds-key:hover:not(.is-active) { transform: translateY(-2px); } .ds-key:active:not(.is-active) { transform: scale(0.94); } .ds-key.is-active { border-color: transparent; background: oklch(0.66 0.19 40); color: #1D1C18; box-shadow: inset 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.28); transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Chip
components.description: A pill on the inset. The tone recolours the TEXT only, via the matching ink token. There is NO dot inside a chip — the component strips a bullet glyph or a nested StatusDot.
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 4px 10px; border: 1px solid #E3E1DA; border-radius: 99px; background: #ECEAE4; color: #5A5850; font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; } .ds-chip--danger { color: oklch(0.491 0.21 25); } .ds-chip--success { color: oklch(0.459 0.17 150); } .ds-chip--warning { color: oklch(0.497 0.15 80); } .ds-chip.is-pressed { background: #FFFFFF; color: #1D1C18; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgba(24,22,16,.05), 0 2px 6px rgba(24,22,16,.06); }

components.name: Cable
components.description: The ONE thing in the system allowed to glow, and only in proportion to live audio. The app writes --oj-cable-signal (0-1) from the shared animation frame; width, opacity and drop-shadow all derive from it. Quiet is 2.5px at 45% with no filter.
components.css: .ds-cable { --oj-cable-signal: 0; fill: none; stroke-linecap: round; stroke-width: calc(2.5px + var(--oj-cable-signal) * 2.5px); opacity: calc(0.5 + var(--oj-cable-signal) * 0.5); filter: drop-shadow(0 0 calc(var(--oj-cable-signal) * 7px) currentColor); transition: stroke-width .03s linear, opacity .03s linear; } .ds-cable--audio { stroke: oklch(0.6 0.12 200); color: oklch(0.6 0.12 200); } .ds-cable--control { stroke: #8F8C82; color: #8F8C82; } .ds-cable.is-quiet { stroke-width: 2.5px; opacity: .45; filter: none; }

narrative.overview: OpenJammer reads the way a well-made piece of hardware reads on a table in front of a room: quiet where it is quiet, loud exactly where the signal is. The canvas is a calm warm neutral under a faint dot grid; nodes are white cards with a single hairline edge, soft layered depth, and ports that are recessed socket wells sunk into the body of the card. Colour is spent only on signal, state and selection, so the loudest thing on screen is always the patch. The system is crafted, immediate and deep: a beginner is making sound in seconds, and the same surface lets an expert drop inside a node and rewire its guts. The whimsy that used to live in a handwritten line now lives in motion, physics and sound-reactive light — a button compresses, a knob resists, a key lights solid accent while it is held, and a cable thickens and glows in proportion to the audio actually passing through it.
keyCharacteristics: Calm ground, loud signal: warm-neutral surfaces, saturated colour only for signal, state and selection.
Everything has weight: buttons compress (.96), pads compress (.94), hover lifts -2px, one spring curve everywhere.
Sound is visible: only cables and meters may glow or pulse. Nothing else glows, ever.
Legible always: UI sans text >= 13px, AA contrast enforced by a test over the token files, mono for exact values.
1px hairline borders and soft layered shadows — no 2px ink, no hard blur-free offset shadow.
Outfit is the one UI voice at every size; JetBrains Mono means exact. No display font in functional UI.
Ports are 18px recessed socket wells INSIDE the node body, in labelled rows: inputs left, outputs right.
Port colour is meaning: audio = teal, control = grey, universal = violet.
Exactly two themes — Light (default) and Dark — as pure value swaps of the same 53 semantic tokens.

rules.name: The Port-Color-Is-Meaning Rule
rules.body: Port and cable colour is never decoration. Teal means audio, grey means control, violet means universal — the port type is the source of truth and the colour follows. Do not spend these colours on anything that is not a port or a cable.

rules.name: The Signal-Not-Brand Rule
rules.body: Success / warning / danger report machine state and always travel with a label or icon. The accent is the brand and the selection. Never style a heading, a surface or a decoration in a state colour, and never use success to mean "selected".

rules.name: The Ink-For-Text Rule
rules.body: A saturated colour is a fill; its *-ink sibling is the text. Fill with accent-danger, write with danger-ink. In BOTH themes --text-on-accent is dark ink #1D1C18, not white: white on the accent measures 3.36:1, dark ink measures 5.08:1 light / 6.27:1 dark. This is why the light accent hover LIFTS instead of darkening.

rules.name: The Outfit-Is-the-Voice Rule
rules.body: One sans does everything at every size in both themes. Weight and size carry hierarchy; a second face never does. There is no display font in functional UI — Caveat is retired and does not return for empty states.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Exact Rule
rules.body: If a value is monospace it can be read, typed, copied or compared character by character, and it carries tabular-nums. Never use mono for emphasis or decoration, and never set an exact value in the sans.

rules.name: The 13px Floor
rules.body: No functional sans text below 13px. The 11px and 9.5px steps exist only for uppercase mono micro-labels with .08em tracking, and they are held to the full 4.5:1 body-text bar rather than a large-text exemption.

rules.name: The Nothing-Glows-Except-Live-Signal Rule
rules.body: drop-shadow and soft coloured halos exist in exactly one component: Cable, driven by the real signal level. Meters brighten and clip-latch. Ports never glow — not on hover, not on connect, not when active. If it glows and it is not carrying audio right now, it is a bug.

rules.name: The Press-Has-Weight Rule
rules.body: A control answers the hand within 120ms and compresses: scale down on press, spring back on release, on the one spring curve. Weight is scale and shadow, never a jump in position.

rules.name: The No-Surprise Rule
rules.body: A control never moves, resizes or reflows under the cursor. Hover feedback is colour, border and — on pads only — a 2px lift. A hit target never oscillates.

rules.name: The One-Ring Rule
rules.body: Focus is --focus-ring on :focus-visible, stacked over whatever shadow the element already has. Not an outline, not a colour change alone, not a second ring style for important controls.

dos: Do keep the ground calm and spend colour on signal, state and selection only.
Do use the four depth roles — raised / overlay / inset / pressed — and let them mean what they say: on it, above it, into it, being hit.
Do give every control weight: motion-fast for colour, motion-spring for transform, press .96 (buttons) or .94 (pads), hover lift -2px on pads and keys.
Do let live audio be the only thing that lights up — cables scale with --oj-cable-signal, meters with --oj-meter-signal.
Do colour ports and cables strictly by type: audio = teal, control = grey, universal = violet.
Do fill with a state colour and write with its *-ink sibling.
Do use one focus ring, on :focus-visible, stacked over the element own shadow.
Do put exact values in JetBrains Mono with tabular-nums, and keep functional sans text at 13px or larger.
Do be honest about state — a transport glyph that waits for the engine, an honest ~15-25ms browser tier, a failure that never hides behind a hopeful spinner.
Do prefer a held, believable sound over a visible glitch when something fails mid-set, and report it without stealing focus.
Do keep every value in a token so the community can reskin the instrument without forking a component.
donts: Don't put a glow on a port — not on hover, not on connect, not when active. Nor on a button, a selection, a node border, or anything not carrying audio right now.
Don't draw a side stripe. The only sanctioned left edge is a timeline clip's track-colour identity, because that stripe is data. Callouts, banners, list rows, menu items and panels get none.
Don't put a dot inside a chip. A chip's tone recolours its text; StatusDot stands beside a label, never inside a pill.
Don't express selection as a fill drench. Selection is an accent edge, plus at most an inset ring or an ink label.
Don't use a display font in functional UI. There is one sans and one mono; Caveat is retired.
Don't write a hard offset shadow (2px 3px 0). Depth is soft and layered; zero-blur offsets are the retired language.
Don't draw a 2px ink border. Borders are 1px hairlines; 1.5px is the maximum, and only on an interactive outline.
Don't use #fff (or any literal) on an accent fill — --text-on-accent is dark ink in both themes for a measured reason.
Don't style a heading, a surface or a decoration in a state colour, and don't use success to mean selected.
Don't ship a component with its own prefers-reduced-motion block — the blanket rule in global.css owns that, with exactly two exemptions.
Don't let a control move, resize or reflow on hover or press.
Don't ever present a wall — no pro ceiling, no dead end. The instrument is infinitely deep and should look like it at every depth.
